speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As we emerge from the pandemic, as we gain invaluable real experiences and as some advanced economies move into the space of Web 3.0, will there be a change to how we envision Singapore as a Smart Nation?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: They can become Singapore's digital economic residents but without the need for citizenship entitlements.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This can bolster Singapore's status as a global hub and, in turn, value-add to our community.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Singapore may be physically limited but virtually unlimited.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: While these incidents were not caused by the Government's system vulnerabilities, the public's confidence in digital transactions with the Government may still, inadvertently, be affected.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Moreover, such transactions with the Government often involve highly sensitive personal data.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Adding on, Singapore is now one of the two Asian countries that have condemned Russia's invasion of Ukraine and imposed sanctions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is a move that we must support but we could now also be an active cyber target.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, what is the Government doing to ensure that our critical infrastructures are robust and Government services are safe and secure for citizens and businesses to transact with?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Lastly, Smart Nation is meant to be a whole-of-nation movement.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Therefore, it will require buy-in and active participation from all levels and segments of our society.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Apart from ensuring that we solve real-life pain points using effective digital solutions that work, the processes, the interfaces, the entire user experience must also be thoughtful, clear and easy to use so that even the less digitally savvy among us will also be encouraged to transact and participate digitally.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Therefore, what is the whole of Government doing to ensure seamless, user-friendly and age-friendly e-services for our people and businesses?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Chairman, Smart Nation requires transformation towards a digital Government, digital economy, digital society and living in a smart city.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A Smart Nation must be more than technology for its own sake.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that it is in its fifth year, how has Smart Nation changed people's lives in Singapore in a real and tangible way and what more can we expect from Smart Nation?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we use Smart Nation initiatives to showcase Singapore's capability to the world?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Chairman, in spite of the greater use of smartphones and the evolution towards digitalisation, many, especially seniors, still prefer speaking to a physical individual at the end of a phone line as compared to a bot or an AI-inspired solution.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This has to be seen within a wider backdrop of still relatively low Internet usership amongst the elderly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Seniors Go Digital initiative that was launched in 2020 helps to provide seniors with basic Internet skills to access Government e-services.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The recent spate of banking scams may have also had a psychological impact among some of our elderly with respect to the security of online or electronic services.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Only last week, the Singapore Police Force said that a new Singpass QR code scam had surfaced, in which victims are asked to fill out surveys in exchange for monetary reward.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Greater public education can go some way to ameliorate these hazards but these scams or security loopholes raise the importance of the availability of alternative channels, such as the maintenance of reliable hotlines, to assure our seniors that access to Government services remain available to them even if they are not online or to seek clarifications promptly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: At the same time, occasional feedback still highlights the trouble people face in getting through Government hotlines.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: An example was in September 2021 when the SAF was roped in to help deal with calls to MOH as some COVID-19-positive Singaporeans could not secure conveyance to a recovery facility in time.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Similar concerns were highlighted during the circuit breaker in 2020 when there was much confusion from businesses about the status of their foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: What lessons have been learnt from these episodes?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And is there a plan to beef up tele-services in spite of this age of digitalisation for better citizen-to-state contact?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What is the progress of our Government’s Smart Nation Plan to create a more seamless and integrated user experience for our citizens and businesses?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, a senior who has been taught to book his medical appointment through the Health Hub app, was told when he arrived at the polyclinic that he will need to download another app to track his queue number for his appointment.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Are there any plans for the relevant agencies from various Ministries to work together and further improve the portal, as well as to raise awareness among more Singaporeans to encourage them to consider doing comprehensive end-of-life planning?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, the pandemic has accelerated the pace and the scale of digitalisation, impacting the way we live, work and play.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Increasingly, we find that to participate in common everyday activities, like accessing information, booking services, making an appointment, making payments, requires digital access and the skills to use digital technology.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Even access to many Government services is digital.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: At the launch of the Smart Nation Initiative in 2014, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan stressed the priority of Smart Nation as, I quote: "Really, it is about people, it is not about technology for technology's sake.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It is about focusing on jobs, quality of life and society", unquote.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Digital inclusion is more than access and affordability; it is about having the skills and confidence to use technology.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: To make digital more inclusive, I believe that we must design digital services and content with the requirements of seniors and persons with disabilities at the centre.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This would make it more intuitive and reduce barriers to use digital services.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And, more importantly, ensure that no one is left behind.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Can the Minister share how we are promoting digital inclusion and bringing people with different needs along our Smart Nation journey?

speaker: Mr Chairman
text: Response from Minister Josephine Teo before Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the limited time available, I will try my best to address Members' concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Sharael Taha asked about the progress of our Smart Nation efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, our Smart Nation is rapidly taking shape and there was no better evidence of this than during the height of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our children could not go to school, but learning did not stop.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many people could not go to their workplaces, but work and meetings continued.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Cinemas and theatres were closed, but we were entertained online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So much of our lives have gone digital.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some of the digital services we use regularly today were nascent only five years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Take the Singpass app, for example, which was only launched in 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Soon, besides the digital IC, our digital driving licence will be accessible on Singpass.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Later this month, Singpass will also allow business owners or their authorised employees to conveniently retrieve basic company information, including awarded Government contracts and shareholders' names.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This makes it easier for them to fulfil such information requests.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members may also have noticed updates on the recent Budget announcements appearing in your Singpass app.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond that, there is an ongoing trial to send citizens personalised information on the Budget through the LifeSG app.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This helps citizens know the support that is most relevant to them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our people can also check their eligibility for various schemes on the Support-Go-Where website.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To date, we have used the Go-Where technology for 16 different purposes, allowing citizens to access key information more easily.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Digitalisation, however, is more than just moving from the physical to the virtual.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The user experience matters, as highlighted by Ms Tin Pei Ling.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And as Ms Hany Soh shared, it is also about unifying multiple touchpoints into a single service journey.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, together with PSD and MOH, we have developed an online portal called My Legacy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The website guides citizens to settle the different components of end-of-life planning, such as lasting power of attorney, advanced care planning and CPF nominations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Information is consolidated in a single platform, enabling a more seamless experience.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some transactions must, however, take place through agency websites, to better protect the users.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One hundred and forty thousand users have used the platform since its release in 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to improve the site and, indeed, other platforms, to achieve greater seamlessness while not compromising security.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Apart from citizens, digitalisation has also led to a sea change for our businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Guided by the Industry Transformation Maps (ITM), new business models, companies and jobs have emerged.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Good jobs have been created for Singaporeans from product managers to algorithm engineers and UI/UX designers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A new wave of entrepreneurs has taken centre stage, from home-based bakers to live streamers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These developments are very much in keeping with our Smart Nation vision, as outlined by Prime Minister Lee during his National Day Rally (NDR) speech in 2017, five years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Then, the Prime Minister said that, and I quote: "Next time I am at a hawker centre, I look forward to paying for my meal with PayNow".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, more than half of all hawkers have adopted e-payments.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What is less well known is that the digitalisation of vouchers and transaction tracking are enabled by RedeemSG, a system developed by GovTech that can be reused for similar voucher programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Another tool is GovWallet, which helps the Government send monies and credits to citizens in a more secure and convenient way.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MINDEF is using GovWallet to disburse NS recognition benefits through the LifeSG app.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The benefits can be used at any of the 164,000 merchants that accept PayNow.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: CPF Board is also using GovWallet to disburse workfare payouts through ATMs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This replaces cheque disbursements and allows us to better serve the unbanked.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our digital foundation has been instrumental to our whole-of-nation COVID-19 response and is constantly being strengthened.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What has been most heartening are the contributions of our vibrant local tech sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One example is Beep Technologies, a local company involved in the deployment of vending machines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We may not have thought too much about what it takes to repurpose vending machines that are more used to dispensing drinks and other regular day-to-day items.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To ensure that the TraceTogether tokens would not break upon being dispensed, Beep engineers used apple pies to test their customised machines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It took many tries before they could get satisfying results.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beep's CEO, 25-year-old Kristoffer Jacek Soh, told me that he founded his company soon after he heard the Prime Minister's NDR speech in 2017 and was inspired.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I hope more young people, like Jacek, will work with us to create our Smart Nation together.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Apart from our local tech sector, tech teams within the Government also played an important role in our COVID-19 response.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many of us have used our national vaccine appointment system.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This was built by a small team of product managers, designers and software engineers, working closely with policymakers, clinicians and ground operators.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They were given just two weeks to get the job done.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Thanks to their efforts, many of us would have taken only minutes to complete our vaccination registration.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As we continue to strengthen our digital foundations, we must be ready to tackle challenges, such as digital inclusion and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In particular, we agree with Ms Jessica Tan that the fast pace of digitalisation can feel daunting, even for people who are willing to learn and try.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, we made a big move to help Singaporeans gain confidence with their digital forays.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides seniors, one of the groups where help has been focused, is, in fact, persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, we are also making digital services more accessible.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, we have translated key Government digital services into more languages.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As more features are onboarded, this will better support citizens who are more comfortable transacting in vernacular languages.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes telephone services, which Mr Pritam Singh mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, when cases spiked in September last year, there was a surge in calls to the COVID-19 emergency hotline.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Within a week, our tech teams set up a call-handling and case management system.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through better information sharing capabilities, productivity of our call agents improved.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Another top priority for us is cyber security, which Ms Tin Pei Ling also highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will speak more about this later during MCI's COS debate.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While we strengthen digital inclusion and cybersecurity, we must look ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Mr Sharael Taha mentioned, there are many exciting opportunities to capture in the next bound of our Smart Nation journey.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even as we speak, the digital future of smart cities, sustainability, finance, education and healthcare is being reshaped.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Technologies, like 5G and autonomous systems, will continue to mature and give us opportunity to reimagine our schools, hospitals, workplaces and even our heartlands.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is much to explore in each of these areas.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will partner citizens in this process as part of our broader SG Together movement.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The newly launched Citizen Co-Creation group will co-develop new solutions with our tech teams in areas, such as smart cities and digital inclusion.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For the third year running, Singapore has topped the IMD-SUTD Smart City Index in 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But we are always keenly aware that what matters most is the satisfaction of our people and businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Satisfaction among businesses has also risen from 64% to 76%.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In today's era of hyper-innovation, every milestone represents just a new beginning.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To stay ahead, we must never stop building new capabilities and never stop seizing new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our Smart Nation is still rapidly taking shape.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through sustained commitment and efforts, we will continue to transform Singaporeans' lives for the better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But there are several advantages to moving earlier on issuance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Second, a digital Sing dollar will allow for the application of more innovative monetary policy, especially with regard to disinflation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While inflation is the current worry, it is not difficult to conceive, with global depopulation, deglobalisation and declining productivity, of the possibility of a reversal to a low-inflation environment a few years down the road.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It would take a few years to roll out the digital currency, making it available to help mitigate the problem of a zero lower bound on nominal interest rates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That said, there are some additional practical concerns for which it will be useful for this House to better understand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: First, to what extent has global best practices in payments innovation, such as those studies in collaboration between the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston and MIT's Project Hamilton Digital Currency initiative, been incorporated into the MAS' own background study?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Second, what are the main inhibitions that MAS holds that prevent sooner issuance?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And third, if there is no urgent need for issuance, what might be the anticipated timeline for a digital Sing dollar?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Their applications were rejected by banks either because of their past criminal records, past investigations for financial-related crimes or are currently under criminal investigation, resulting in their bank accounts being frozen.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Members of this House would agree that access to basic banking facilities is essential in today's digitalised society.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: These individuals are deprived of basic banking activities, such as receiving their salaries.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Employers do not usually agree to deposit into their family's bank accounts and are unwilling to pay them in cash.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They also have difficulty receiving Government cash benefits, like GST Vouchers – Cash.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Individuals with past criminal records have paid their dues to society and such a deprivation can be an impediment in their efforts to turn over a new leaf.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Similarly, individuals under investigation are deprived of the operation of the maxim "innocent until proven guilty".

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Minister what are the limitations on such accounts?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Will the functions of such accounts vary on a case-by-case basis assessment by the banks?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Additionally, will the pool of eligible individuals for these accounts include persons who are currently under investigation?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This may emerge as a growing problem owing to the increase in bank accounts being frozen during investigations into financial crimes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Owing to the time sensitivity of this matter, can I ask the Minister what is the progress of the roll-out of these limited purpose bank accounts?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Is it generally available to all affected applicants yet?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If not, when will it remain available generally?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Assoc Prof Jamus Lim for his interest and comments on a digital Singapore dollar.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS has been among the central banks at the forefront of experiments with central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), especially wholesale CBDCs, starting over five years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has been actively engaged in the international discourse on CBDCs among policymakers, industry and academia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several other central banks have taken the same view for now, such as the US Federal Reserve, Bank of Canada and the Reserve Bank of Australia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The reasons typically offered for issuing retail CBDCs are not very relevant to MAS and Singapore at this juncture.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some of the reasons usually offered are that CBDCs can ensure financial inclusion or enable cheaper and faster payments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Financial inclusion is not a significant problem in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And electronic payments in Singapore have also become pervasive, seamless and efficient.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we are also linking up this infrastructure with those abroad, which will open up more cross-border electronic payment solutions over time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Government transfers are disbursed efficiently through digital means, including through the last two years of the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the payments system is becoming even more innovative and competitive, as more payments service providers are being admitted through the Payment Services Act and the new digital banks begin operating.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In short, we are using improvements in payment technology and competition to achieve our objectives of cheap and fast payments for all, using existing forms of central bank-backed money.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This does not mean that MAS has ruled out introducing a retail CBDC at some stage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The case for a CBDC could strengthen if foreign digital currencies become more widely used locally, although we are far away from that situation today.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Innovative CBDC applications may also make them more attractive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS, therefore, continues to build up its technological and institutional capabilities in the CBDC space.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It also organised a Global CBDC Challenge last year to surface innovative technology solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Issuing a retail CBDC will not be a minor decision.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are important risks and uncertainties that come with creating a new form of money.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS has set these out clearly in a paper that it published on the topic in November 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A digital Singapore dollar must be secure and robust once it is implemented.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The banking system needs to be able to adapt to its introduction, and monetary and financial stability cannot be compromised.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is a complex undertaking and careful practical experimentation alongside industry players will be necessary, if we do decide to proceed with a retail CBDC at some stage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the second cut by Mr Gerald Giam, last year, MAS engaged the major retail banks on initiatives to enhance financial inclusion for ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And since January this year, the banks have been offering, as part of a pilot exercise, limited purpose bank accounts to persons whom banks have assessed may pose higher risks of being implicated in financial crimes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These include ex-offenders and those under investigations or pending charges for financial crimes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The functionalities and safeguards for limited purpose bank accounts are designed to enable individuals to meet their basic banking needs, like receiving salaries and paying bills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To mitigate risks of abuse, the accounts are subjected to enhanced monitoring measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, banks will check that individuals are only receiving funds from specified sources which had been agreed upon at account-opening, including salary payments from employers, Government disbursements and insurance payouts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These functionalities and safeguards will be adjusted, as necessary, after the current pilot.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The limited purpose bank accounts will address the needs of most ex-offenders and persons under investigations or facing charges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: However, there may be a small number of individuals whom banks have assessed to pose unacceptable risks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, this might include individuals who have committed serious crimes involving the violation of targeted financial sanctions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS will continue to work with the Singapore Police Force on further ways to enable financial inclusion for individuals who have been involved in financial crimes, while ensuring that the risks are properly managed.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They cited cost of living, stressful education system and lack of quality time as their top concerns.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can we build cultural norms and an environment that are more family-friendly in Singapore?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe we need to tackle three interdependent fronts together for family centricity – at home, at work and in the society.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such flexible remote working arrangements have provided a space for more parents to spend more time with their children while still attending to work.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While there are, certainly, those who had to cope with more childcare and work burdens, many residents shared with me that it has given them a chance to make adjustments and see their children more.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, flexible work practices and family-friendly workplaces were highlighted as one of the key themes that emerged from "Building a Singapore that is Made-for-Families" in the Emerging Stronger Conversations.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a society, we also begin to appreciate that the flexible work arrangements can be a reality, with adjustments to expectations and mindsets during this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know I sound like a broken record as here I am again asking for the Government to provide childcare sick leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Working parents need this, especially during this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Our frontline and essential workers and those who cannot work from home need this, especially during this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The Public Service already gives officers childcare sick leave and it is on a per-child basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Civil servants are using this childcare sick leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If the Government feels that childcare sick leave is important for the people who work for us, then why is it not important for the people we serve?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Let us also not use flexible work arrangements to justify not providing childcare sick leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If this reason is true, then why do civil servants who have flexible work arrangements also have childcare sick leave?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Will the Government consider providing childcare sick leave for all working parents on a per-child basis?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I have raised this issue many times and I hope the reply would not be the same again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: An NUS study found that children whose fathers take paternity leave are significantly less likely to have behavioural issues.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The study also found that these families have less internal conflict, lower likelihood of maternal depression, more marital satisfaction and more father-child closeness.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The case for paternity leave cannot be stronger.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: However, the study also found that fathers in more labour-intensive jobs, such as machine operators and cleaners, were half as likely to take paternity leave as fathers working as legislators, senior officials and managers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We need to do more to help lower-income fathers take their paternity leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Why should they be denied the time to spend with their babies?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Government conduct a targeted study on the barriers to taking paternity leave for lower-income workers, look into policies to increase their usage of paternity leave and also look into incentivising employers who support their employees to take their paternity leave?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, more than 60% of those surveyed in the Institute of Policy Studies online polls revealed their concerns over an increased suspicion among people of different social backgrounds as a result of COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Even though bigoted behaviour seen in public and hateful online comments may be limited to only a small section of our society, such acts of denigration are, unfortunately, magnified on social media.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Our foreign friends feel the brunt of xenophobia keenly.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Some have left due to border restrictions, whilst others are considering their options, for fear of growing nativism in Singapore society.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Xenophobic acts threaten our multicultural way of life that we fought hard to foster.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Close to a third of the workforce in Singapore is made up of foreigners from different corners of the world, to sustain our economic and caregiving activities, complementing our local force.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: We, ourselves, began as an immigrant society and our forefathers came from different backgrounds, settling down in Singapore and calling it home.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their cuts.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Family is a key source of strength and support, especially in tough times.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As such, supporting Singaporeans who want to start and raise families remains the Government's top priority.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I will speak about three Government strategies to build a more resilient population in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, building a Singapore that is Made For Families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, moderating the impact of low birth rates and ageing through selective immigration.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, strengthening our local workforce and complementing it with a foreign workforce, to grow opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, we continue to support Singaporeans who wish to start and expand their families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh had filed a cut about our strategies to encourage Singaporeans to get married and have children, given our low Total Fertility Rate (TFR).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While this was 3% lower than in 2019 before COVID-19 struck, the fall was less than we had feared.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But it remains lower than the pre-COVID-19 period.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: TFR is a measure of births per female of child-bearing age.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While the number of births remained similar, the number of such females decreased over the same period, hence, TFR increased.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Raising birth rates is key to tackling Singapore's long-term demographic challenges.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, getting married and having children are personal decisions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We know that aspirations for Marriage and Parenthood (M&P) remain high.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will redouble our efforts to support Singaporeans who choose to get married and have children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Strong and stable families are the bedrock of our society.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are committed to fostering a supportive environment for them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We held the Emerging Stronger Conversations last year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over 300 participants gave suggestions on how to better support families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the Conversations, which Miss Cheng Li Hui had asked about in her cut, some young couples shared their concerns about having children during a pandemic.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To reassure couples to proceed with their parenthood plans, we introduced the one-off Baby Support Grant.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One such couple is Danial and Syaqilah, who got engaged, married and had their first child all within two years.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They initially planned to have their first child only after moving into their Build-to-Order (BTO) flat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, they decided to go ahead as there was no perfect time to have a baby.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Baby Isa was born in August 2021 and they were glad that the Baby Support Grant helped with their transition into parenthood.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Danial and Syaqilah showed us that COVID-19 need not discourage us from making important life plans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Other couples highlighted concerns about housing and the BTO pipeline, as many aspire to have their own home before they start families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui filed a cut on how the Government can support such couples to access affordable housing, amidst disruptions due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are pushing hard to complete our BTO projects as planned.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Couples waiting for their BTO flats to be completed can rent a flat at highly subsidised rates under HDB's Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To better meet demand, HDB is ramping up the supply of PPHS flats with 800 additional units.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With more people marrying later, fertility health will become more of an issue and must be taken seriously.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the Conversations, couples with fertility issues spoke about their challenges.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We must continue to support and encourage them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes encouraging couples to understand and address potential fertility issues earlier, and workplaces to be more supportive.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also introduce new funding support for certain types of Pre-implantation Genetic Testing for Singaporean couples to address the concerns that some couples have over genetically-transmitted diseases.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will share more details at a later time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To give every child a good start in life, we will continue to invest heavily in promoting good health and education from the early years.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will further support the physical, mental and cognitive well-being of children and their families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Child and Maternal Health and Well-Being Taskforce is developing a five-year national strategy to address this.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli will provide more details during MOH's COS.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are continuing to make quality preschools more affordable and accessible.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, a working couple earning $8,000 per month pays $280 per month when they send their child for full-day childcare at an Anchor Operator preschool.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is 40% lower than the $470 per month they had to pay before preschool subsidies were enhanced in 2020.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Lower-income working families pay as low as $3 a month at such preschools.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By around 2025, eight in 10 preschoolers can have a place in a quality, affordable Government-supported preschool.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government is currently reviewing our measures to improve the M&P journey.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Louis Ng suggested incentivising employers to increase usage of paternity leave, particularly among lower-income workers and providing childcare sick leave for all working parents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I fully agree that parents need more flexibility and time away from work to care for their children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes whether supervisors are supportive of fathers taking leave and whether colleagues are willing to cover their duties.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In some labour-intensive jobs, employers may be less willing to let fathers go on extended leave due to the challenge of finding covering arrangements.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, supporting the caregiving needs of parents must be balanced with the manpower and operational needs of employers, particularly our Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs), some of which may still be grappling with the effects of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To address the pressure of managing work and parenting commitments, we have to go beyond Government policies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We need to come together as a whole of society to build a more family-friendly Singapore for a more sustainable approach.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Ms Ng Ling Ling pointed out, a pro-family workplace culture is important.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Around the world, the pandemic has prompted many to rethink where, how and why we work.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The US has experienced the "Great Resignation" – a phenomenon in which scores of employees have quit their jobs as they rethink priorities and search for better working conditions or more fulfilling careers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While we have not had a "Great Resignation", there are clear indications that Singaporeans are paying more attention to whether employers support work-life balance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Recent surveys suggest that workers in Singapore value employers who enable them to manage both their career and family commitments.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling said that mindsets must change, I agree.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Prof Hoon Hian Teck also filed a cut about work-from-home arrangements to bolster family life.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Adopting flexible work arrangements and prioritising employee well-being are not only good for workers and, consequently, for families; in the post-pandemic world, these are going to be the key to firms' competitiveness, productivity and ability to recruit and retain talent.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I want to emphasise that there is a distinction between FWAs and work-from-home (WFH).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: People often use these terms interchangeably, but they are not the same.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Not all job types are suitable for WFH, but all job types can accommodate some form of FWA, depending on the nature of the job.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Other forms of FWAs include flexi-time and flexi-load arrangements.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Every organisation, big or small, can consider adopting the FWAs that best suit their employees' needs and their business operations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Pre-pandemic, Singtel already provided their employees FWA options, such as telecommuting, flexi-time and part-time work.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singtel also offers "Flexi Family Leave" – five days of leave for birthdays, childcare, adoption and family emergencies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We, ultimately, require the partnership of the wider community to build a Singapore that is Made For Families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We launched the Made For Families brand mark in June 2020 to assure families of support from the Government and community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To date, more than 90 businesses, organisations and community groups have adopted it and we hope more will take action and join us.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Together, we will support and celebrate all families at every stage of their journey.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli will share more details on our plans for the year ahead.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, I will touch on moderating the impact of low birth rates and ageing through selective immigration.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, our population continues to age, which has implications for our workforce and society.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To moderate the impact of low birth rates and ageing, we take in a carefully controlled number of new citizens and Permanent Residents each year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are selective about who we grant Permanent Residency (PR) and, subsequently, citizenship to.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many of our new immigrants share family ties with Singaporeans while others have studied, worked or lived here for some time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These numbers are similar to pre-COVID-19 levels and higher, when compared to 2020, due to the easing of travel restrictions and safe management measures, which previously slowed down in-person processes for the grant of citizenship or PR.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our third strategy is to remain fully committed to supporting Singaporeans to seize new opportunities at various stages of their careers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, we do not have sufficient local manpower to meet the needs of businesses.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To generate the quality and range of jobs to meet Singaporeans’ aspirations, we need a diverse pool of foreign manpower to complement our local workforce.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We must remain open towards complementary talent from overseas who bring valuable skills, networks and expertise.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They can contribute to the development of emerging sectors where we need more time to grow local capabilities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As our economic needs evolve, we must ensure the right balance and complementarity between local and foreign manpower.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Tan See Leng will be providing more details during MOM’s COS.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have people from all over the world joining us.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many of them contribute to Singapore and some have come to regard Singapore as their home, adding to our diversity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are proud of our diversity in Singapore, which is bound by a strong sense of community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In many other societies, COVID-19 has further widened social and economic divides.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also seen greater occurrences of xenophobic sentiments and behaviours around the world.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Ms Foo Mee Har has emphasised, we must guard against such sentiments and continue to strengthen our ties with one another.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is especially important for Singapore as a multi-cultural society.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fostering social integration and cohesion requires a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As individuals, each of us has a part to play.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Let us be inclusive, patient and help newcomers to adapt to local norms.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Similarly, foreigners here should make the effort to adapt and integrate over time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also worked with partners on initiatives to help foreigners settle in and understand local norms and culture.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Another example is how we worked with Singaporeans as part of the Citizen’s Workgroup for the Singapore Citizenship Journey (SC Journey) to explore, discuss and create content to update the SC Journey for our new citizens.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The SC Journey will include the co-created content for newcomers to better learn and appreciate aspects of life in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ultimately, we recognise that integration may take some time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We must cherish the unity in diversity that Singapore has, which has helped everyone to rally together.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will press on to build a more inclusive and brighter future for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With many Singaporeans still aspiring to start and raise families, we will continue to build a Singapore that is Made For Families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also continue to review our population strategies to ensure that they remain relevant to our needs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Together, we will build a more resilient population and keep Singaporeans fully at the heart of our population strategies.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In this Budget, we are looking for ways to cut costs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The most effective way to cut costs is to streamline the Government structure.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We should ensure that the money is applied efficiently.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For each social purpose, there should be only one channel or platform.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PA is more like a political structure, led by political appointees and volunteers.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thus, it is not clear whether it is serving the purpose, the people or the ruling party.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If it is not political, to avoid duplicating resources, we should either integrate PA into MCCY or put all community engagement activities at MCCY into PA.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We should turn our community engagement into asset-light activities and stop incurring huge development expenditures on building new community centres.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Instead, we should free up the land and resources tied up in the community centres and other facilities and reallocate those resources to other social needs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We can also potentially do more with the same dollar if we reorganise some activities among MOE, MOM and MSF.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: SkillsFuture courses that do not result in better jobs should be dropped.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The MRC will focus on strengthening our social and financial compact, and oversee social and family development, scholarship and bursary programmes, CPF, a national healthcare scheme, a new unemployment insurance and lifelong fulfilment programmes for the benefit of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Mr Chairman, the onset of COVID-19 shows the benefits of digital service delivery, which allows citizens to be served despite the need to avoid physical interactions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: However, there is a significant group of citizens who may find it challenging to transact with the Government using digital platforms.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: For these citizens, who can also include those in low-income households, they may have added difficulties in navigating Government services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Can PSD share what are the key efforts made by the Public Service to better integrate services, with citizens and businesses at the centre?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: How does the Public Service ensure that those who are digitally less-savvy are not left behind as the Public Service digitalises to its core?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Digital transformation has accelerated as Singaporeans learned to connect with others, including hawkers and retailers, from their homes in this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Many of my residents, including senior citizens, now interact with me over online Meet-the-People sessions and livestreamed constituency events.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Technology is important as a touchpoint between the Government and citizens.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The high and increasing figures in the Annual Survey on Satisfaction with Government Digital Services are commendable.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is also heartening to see that 97% of citizens and 95% of businesses were satisfied with the digital solutions rolled out by the Government during the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, there are still many opportunities to tap on.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The centralisation of functions on a single platform – like the Singpass and TraceTogether Apps – is helpful and should be further developed.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If we can seamlessly integrate the services from different Government agencies using a single platform and a common pool of citizens’ data, we can utilise AI to better anticipate individual citizens' needs and push services to those who may not be aware of schemes applicable to them.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Meanwhile, episodes involving the private sector have demonstrated the risks that we need to manage while going digital.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The compromise of personal access details through scams, service outages due to backend technical issues, and data breaches are something we need to look out for.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How does the Public Service intend to leverage technology to deliver its services better and faster to citizens, or to improve its own productivity?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: To ensure that our public officers can continue to respond decisively to global developments, they will need to remain adaptable through constant upskilling and new experiences, so that they can serve Singapore more effectively through this period of significant global shifts.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How will the Government support their growth and career development?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: To continually attract the best Singaporean talents to serve Singapore, our Public Service will need to evolve in line with global trends.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Will we allow our Public Service officers to go on a year-long workcation?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As our workforce ages and we gradually extend our statutory retirement and re-employment ages, it will be increasingly important for us to also extend the lifelong employability of our Public Service officers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can the Minister provide an update on the efforts on this front?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We should strive towards a future where officers can have two, or even three fulfilling careers in the whole of Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chairman, let me first thank the various Members for their useful suggestions and concerns for the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I would also like to thank all my public officers for all the hard work that they have done over the last two years, in particular.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I am sure Members of the House will agree with me that, over the last two years, the Public Service has really pulled together to do three things concurrently and to do three things well.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, to maintain our current operations to make sure that all our services to our people and our country continue to run smoothly amidst the crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, to run crisis operations, we had to invent on the fly many of the new things that we had to do to cope with the ever-evolving virus situation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To this end, we had to even cross-deploy officers to new roles.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Third, our public officers continue to plan for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: That, notwithstanding the crisis and the current operations, we established those conditions for us to emerge stronger and to distinguish ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For all these reasons of running the three – current operations, crisis operations and future operations – I would like to thank all my public officers for all the hard work and determination.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Chairman, we have heard various suggestions on how the Public Service can do better.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Indeed, we agree with the Members that we not rest on our laurels.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Public Service is always looking for better ways to make sure that we can use our finite resources and manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Perhaps, I would just like to give some examples of how the Public Service has done over the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The first example of how we have tried to do better and use our resources more efficiently is from GovTech.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The GoWhere platform supports our location- and eligibility-based queries.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As part of our COVID-19 response, the Public Service agencies use GoWhere as a channel to provide citizens with the locations of key services, starting with the collection of masks via Mask GoWhere in 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Another example is our establishment of the Centres of Excellence, or what we called CentExs, by leveraging on the agencies with critical science, technology and engineering experience to build deep technical expertise and pool specialised resources across the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, JTC is designated as the Centre of Excellence (CentExs) for facilities management and is progressively consolidating the facility management contracts for public sector-owned buildings under one integrated contract.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: JTC also provides its expertise to guide the various agencies on how to structure those contracts in order for us to get value-for-money.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: A third example would be how we are bringing together more services under our Integrated Public Service Centres, or what we called ServiceSG Centres now, which has integrated and delivered a wide range of public services across different agencies under one roof.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Citizens can now also conduct video conferences with officers from different agencies in one place.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Going forward, we will extend the pilot to establish more ServiceSG Centres within Community Centres (CCs).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The first of two such ServiceSG Centres have opened in Nee Soon Central and Kampong Chai Chee CCs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Likewise, for businesses, we have developed the one-stop GoBusiness portal to provide easy-to-use, seamless and relevant services, as well as create a more pro-business environment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This year, business owners can expect a new GoBusiness dashboard that will allow them to track their licence applications and access various e-Advisers for recommendations on grants and other services.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On Mr Melvin Yong's point about developing the competencies of our public officers, that is, indeed, one of our focuses going forward, especially when our public officers have a longer career working lifespan.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are various things that we intend to do for our public officers for their career development, in order to build up their capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We intend to have greater porosity among the public sector, people and private sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But within the public sector itself, we also intend to have greater porosity among different agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Talent Attachment Programme (TAP) has been expanded.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In fact, over the last year, we have almost doubled the number of people who have gone on a Talent Attachment Programme (TAP).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These are programmes that allow our public officers to be attached to organisations outside the Public Service, so that they can establish the connections, bring back new ideas for us in the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to look for more opportunities for this porosity of exchanges, so that we can get the best ideas from the public sector, the people sector and elsewhere beyond the Public Service, including international organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Within the public sector itself, we also want to make sure our officers – even if they are performing the same function in different agencies – get opportunities to be posted across to different agencies because, even within the same functional areas, no two agencies perform the function in exactly the same way and we can, of course, learn from one another.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond this, we want to make sure that as we go forward in the way we govern, we will work closely and closer with the organisations beyond the public sector.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We want to broaden our connections with the organisations beyond the public sector.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We want to tap on their capacities and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We do this for a very simple reason.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We want our public officers to, first, deeply understand the partners that they are working with so that when they make the rules and regulations, they have a deep understanding of the people and organisations that they are serving.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second reason for us to do this is because we want our public officers to make sure that they continue to learn from the sectors and organisations beyond the Public Service, and bring back new ideas, bring back new connections, to enrich the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Last but not least, in a crisis like COVID-19, what we have demonstrated is that we depend not just on the whole-of-Government capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In fact, we depend on the whole-of-nation capacity when our public officers have to go forth and make the adjustments for the crisis management operations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They bring in organisations, volunteers beyond the Public Service and that helps to add to our Public Service capacities and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On Mr Leong Mun Wai's point to streamline the Government organisations, perhaps, I would like to let Mr Leong Mun Wai know that, indeed, we have already done many of the things that he suggested.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Where it is logical, we bring services and facilities together.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Good examples of this include the Heartbeat@Bedok and Our Tampines Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Where it is logical and saves us money and resources, we bring different agencies under one roof so that we can save money for our country and save manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On the other hand, we also have an asset-light model.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, in the new generation of CCs, like the one in Potong Pasir and the upcoming Woodleigh development, we have integrated the CCs with the commercial developments so that we can operate with an asset-light model.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But a more important point that Mr Leong Mun Wai asked is: what is the purpose of the People's Association (PA)?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The role of the PA is to help us build up our social capital in peacetime.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, during the COVID-19 crisis, where did we get the extra capacity to reach out to do our vaccination operations, to distribute the masks, to distribute the sanitisers?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Where did we get the people to go and reach out to the people who are in isolation in their homes?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Without these capabilities and capacities, I am not sure that we will be able to achieve the various things that we have been able to achieve during our crisis operations to manage the ongoing COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, for these two years, what we have built up, assiduously, over peacetime – these social bonds, this trust, this deep network – to help our people and reach out, have been invaluable to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And that is not something that many other countries have because perhaps, many other countries take it for granted that the social bonds will be there.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In fact, Mr Leong Mun Wai might also like to know that PA works very closely with MCCY.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In fact, the CED of PA works very closely with the Permanent Secretary of MCCY – their budgets come together.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On Mr Leong Mun Wai's suggestions about having the MOE work with MSF seamlessly, I would also like to inform Mr Leong that I have been involved in this effort on both sides.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Why is ECDA an agency that is reporting to both MOE and MSF?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Because ECDA performs the role of taking care of the preschool children with both the education component by MOE and the care component by MSF.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is how we flexibly configure our organisations in order to meet the needs of our people.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, it is not a "stove-pipe" mindset that we adopt, going into how we structure an organisation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But having said that, we will be the first to admit that, as circumstances change and evolve, we will continue to evolve our organisations and structures to best meet today's needs and also to anticipate tomorrow's challenges and we will continue to do this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I will be the first one to say that the Public Service is not perfect.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On that note, I would like to thank all the Members for your various suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If you have other suggestions on how we can do better as a Public Service, we welcome your suggestions and we will certainly look into them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It is good to know that there have been good progress and achievements.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Given the advancement of technology, as we move into Web 3.0, as preferences and habits change amongst our people and business models as well, and, with new use cases, I would like to ask whether there has been any update on the vision of our Smart Nation initiative.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Also, would e-residency be already on the agenda?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling had asked the question of e-residency.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is not necessarily a question for SNDGG to address.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MHA oversees immigration matters, MOM oversees work passes for foreign nationals.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If it is merely to work or to provide services without being physically here, actually, for Singapore, that is already happening and there are no impediments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If it is to enter Singapore freely, for example, not to have the same kind of restrictions for visas and so on, again, Singapore's openness makes it quite questionable what this e-residency confers in terms of additional benefits.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If it is then to offer access to things like healthcare or other services that residents enjoy, we have to ask the question what obligations the e-residents should be expected to fulfil.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Are the potential e-residents asking to pay taxes in Singapore?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Are the e-residents saying that they agree to be bound by Singapore's laws?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And in any case, if they are not in Singapore, how would those obligations be enforceable?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then, to the question of the benefits to Singapore of offering such e-residency.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Of course, for Singapore-based companies, one could make the argument that they can access the talents, a much wider pool, which they can already today.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But can I just focus my clarification on low-income parents who, very often, cannot work-from-home or they have different kinds of FWAs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I agree with the Minister, I hope that employers can be more supportive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But I think we know, from the NUS study, this is not happening on the ground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, could I ask the Government, specifically for low-income parents, what are we doing to help them to have some time off when their child is sick or, at least, when their child is born?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As far as low-income workers and employees are concerned, they, too, are on our radar.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They are parents, just like others, and we would want to make sure that they have sufficient time to look after their children.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, let us study this together with MOM.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Whatever we do must be something that is practical and feasible, given the nature of their work.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because, very often, they do have to be there, physically present.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And then the question is whether or not the employer has got other people to cover for them if they take time off.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I think what the Member can take away today is that they are on our radar and, just like any other parent, we would want them to have sufficient time with their children.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.
